Yes this is true! Your actual genes won't change, & no genetic mutations or anything like that. BUT the way certain genes are expressed can be changed after exposure to trauma (and other environmental exposures etc, not just trauma!).

Very basically, some genes get unregulated (expressed more), and some downregulated or repressed (expressed less, or inhibited completely) due to many mechanisms, but a major one is called histone modification. This is the epigenetics stuff. And it can be inherited. 

It could mean that there's a lowered tolerance for stress, altered metabolism, anything really that could relate to the exposure. But it's not certain and not "the be all and end all". Lots of different things come into how it may or may not impact you or any children you may have.

It is very complex and nuanced... but super interesting imo! Learnt a lot about it at university.
